title: Another inquest announced
article: A day after a coroner's inquest looking into the death of Colin Tremeer concluded, the Coroner's Service announced an inquest will be held next spring to look into another apparent drug overdose death of a man who had been in police custody in Kelowna.
On Aug. 7--two days after Tremeer died--Kelowna RCMP encountered Michael Stein driving erratically at the Glenmore Plaza on Kane Road.
When they pulled him over, he "ducked down" under the dashboard for a couple of seconds before popping up and placing his hands on the wheel of the car.

His female companion told police Stein shoved a ball of crack cocaine in his mouth before police detained him, an information to obtain (ITO) a search warrant indicates, and he later spit the remains of it onto the floor of the police car and swallowed part of it.

As an officer drove Stein to the RCMP station, he suspected Stein may be attempting to ingest drugs and pulled over. Stein told the officer that he ate some crack, and the officer radioed the police dispatcher to request paramedics meet him at the RCMP detachment, the ITO indicates.

His behaviour became more erratic at the RCMP station, and, while being placed on a gurney, the ITO indicates Stein went into full cardiac arrest. Paramedics revived him, but he died in hospital on Aug. 16.

At the three-day inquest scheduled to get underway May 21, 2008, coroner Bruce Chamberlayne and a five-person jury will publicly hear evidence from witnesses in order to determine the facts surrounding the death. The jury will get to make recommendations aimed at preventing deaths under similar circumstances in the future.
